title: Member Hardship Clause — Flat Allowance on Late RideLink Settlements
content:
A late Non-Emergency Medical Transportation trip settlement may carry a flat allowance that follows the member's eligibility category and recorded household income.

**Rule.** A settlement that is late carries a flat late-settlement allowance set by the member's active Medicaid Managed Care Membership: the full late allowance of 15.00 USD when the membership is in Prairie Ridge ABD Care or Prairie Ridge Dual Complete and records household income at or below the poverty percent of 100 percent of the federal poverty level; the partial late allowance of 10.00 USD when exactly one of those two holds; and no allowance when neither holds. A settlement that is not late carries no allowance. The allowance is added to the settlement as a flat amount.

**When a settlement is late.** A settlement is late when more than the level's reimbursement payment days have passed from the start of the settlement clock — the date the records show the trip could first be settled — to the settlement date. The payment days are 30 on RideLink Mileage Reimbursement, RideLink Ambulatory Sedan and RideLink Door-to-Door Assist, and 0 on RideLink Transit Pass, RideLink Wheelchair Van and RideLink Stretcher Van.

## Truth table, for a late settlement

| Membership in Prairie Ridge ABD Care or Prairie Ridge Dual Complete | Recorded household income at or below 100 percent | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 15.00 USD |
| Yes | No | 10.00 USD |
| No | Yes | 10.00 USD |
| No | No | None |

## Cases

*Hypothetical members:*

- Prairie Ridge Dual Complete, income 90 percent, settlement 40 days after the clock started on a 30-day level: late, 15.00 USD.
- Prairie Ridge Family Care, income 100 percent, settlement 35 days after the clock started on a 30-day level: late, 10.00 USD.
- Prairie Ridge ABD Care, income 80 percent, settlement 30 days after the clock started on a 30-day level: not late, no allowance.
